elements.evidence: "(c) Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time"

elements.element: 30 days' written notice for Customer termination
Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on such termination
elements.evidence: "Contractor shall refund prepaid fees on a pro-rata basis for the period after the effective date of termination"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: Agreement has no committed term ("shall continue until terminated by either party"); Contractor's at-will right remains confined to "At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding" — the condition is demonstrably absent, and Contractor cannot exit at will while an SOW runs."
"upon 30 days' written notice" — shorter than the 60–90 day fallback band (more favourable to us, but not the fallback term)

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed on Customer; condition absent

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term, on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "Contractor may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon 90 days' advance written notice" — 90 days' notice present but not limited to end of a term (limited instead to no outstanding SOW)

reasons: The preferred level is complete: (c) grants Customer a 30-day written-notice convenience exit with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and no committed term exists, so the 'no Vendor convenience right during a committed term' condition is satisfied by the existing 'no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding' gate.

Minimality fails: extending Contractor's notice period from fifteen (15) days to '90 days' imports the fallback's Vendor-notice requirement, which the preferred level does not require once Contractor's at-will right is fenced to periods with no outstanding SOW; changing 'either party' to 'Contractor' alone (or leaving (a) untouched) would have sufficed.

The added definition '"Customer" means Company.' is unnecessary boilerplate — the inserted sentence could simply have used the existing defined term 'Company', avoiding a new alias in a document that otherwise never uses 'Customer'.

Intent is preserved: the material-breach mechanic, fee-through-termination entitlement and assignment of Works in progress in (b) are untouched, and no undefined term or dangling mechanic results (the new alias is defined in-line).
